chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Sonny Clay's bands, Charlie Green's sleeping sickness and Jazz Carson
summary: Spikes discusses Clay's early groups, Charlie Green who fell asleep playing, Davidson called Big Boy, and Jazz Carson who married in China.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: From 1918 to '20, Sonny Clay worked with a clarinetist called Charlie Green.
Yeah. Charlie Green. Yeah. Charlie Green used to play with me. He was...he had kind of sleeping disease. He be sittin' up playing the clarinet and he'd go sound asleep.
Yeah, they call that narcolepsy--when you can't stay awake.

Well, I must have different, you know. I went... you know, when I went to sleep this morning, it was a quarter after six. I laid there all night long, read the paper, read the Bible, read the songbooks, read the...heh heh...everything I could get.
Sonny Clay's Eccentric Harmony Six...uh, in 1922, had William Hansett on cornet, Archie Grant on trombone and piano, Cash Green--which they say may be Charles Green...
Theo. Bonner on saxophone, W.B. Woodman, trombone, and Sonny Clay, piano and drums, saxophones and various instruments. He played a lot of different things, huh?

Well, I never know him to play saxophone. He played, I think, marimba and piano and...and, let's see, what else Sonny played? I think he played drum...I think he played drums in my brother's orchestra. I think he was a drummer when he first come here from Tucson.
And it mentions Harold Lee on drums. And "Leonard Davidson worked with Clay frequently..."
Yeah, yeah, Davidson worked for me. He's a big fella...saxophone player. We call him "Big Boy." 'at's all.
Oh. Let's see. Personnel: Ernest Coycault, trumpet; Leon White, trombone; James "Jazz" Carson, tenor saxophone.

Oh, yeah, Carson. Carson played for me...with me a long time. He went to China with a group, and he married a Chinee woman over there, and he...when the war broke out, they came back, and he's got five or six little old Chinee babies. 'Course that's been fifteen, twenty years ago. I guess they're all grown. I don't know whether Carson's
around here or where he is since that. He brought his Chinee wife and ever' body back--all his kids.
